To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the physicality of the interaction and the digital information that it triggers, can be used to promote active learning.
(i) children can be motivated to explore and interact with a digitally augmented physical space, and (ii) this can lead to active, creative and collaborative learning.

(1) children are able to engage with a digitally augmented physical space; (2) the space is able to support a diversity of learning styles; (3) children are able interact with the space in a variety of ways; (4) the space is engaging and motivating; (5) the space can be used in different learning contexts; (6) the space can support different levels of learning; and (7) the space can facilitate learning in different ways.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how we can design learning environments where children can learn through physical interaction, where the physical and digital are integrated and where the learning experience can be augmented through digitally generated information.
the design of digitally augmented physical spaces for learning.
the question of what happens when we get physical with digital technologies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of digitally augmented physical spaces can be a very powerful way to support learning, but that it is not without its challenges.
children's active engagement with the physical world is facilitated when the physical world is digitally augmented.
the physicality and the interactivity of the digital information is a key ingredient for promoting active learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the learning benefits of our approach can be explained in terms of the physical and the digital, and how they are combined in a variety of ways.

children are able to engage more effectively with the digital world when they are able to interact with the 'physical' world, and that this can be achieved by designing digitally augmented physical spaces.
the design of learning experiences that exploit the physicality and the digitality of the world around us can promote active and playful engagement with the world.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the design and development of digitally augmented physical spaces is not trivial, as it involves the integration of a diversity of technologies and requires a careful consideration of the physical and the digital in order to promote learning.
the learning experience can be significantly enhanced when the physical and digital aspects of the interaction are well balanced and when the interaction is playful and fun.
the physical world and digital information are not mutually exclusive and can be integrated in novel ways, that can be beneficial for learning.
